meta.title: Kalachowkicha Mahaganpati
meta.foundedNote: 1956 is reported by contemporary FPJ coverage; an original founding document was not inspected.
meta.intro: Kalachowkicha Mahaganpati is the Ganesh festival of Kalachowki Vibhag Sarvajanik Utsav Mandal on Dattaram Lad Marg. Its photograph series now reaches from a 2013 display to the 2026 arrival, showing seated, standing and multi-armed forms across changing years. Marathi and English reporting also documents neighborhood service, processional labor and the 2026 fatal electrical accident near the pandal. Its identity remains separate from Kalachowki's similarly named Maharaja and other local mandals.

paragraphs.text: The Mahaganpati belongs to Kalachowki Vibhag Sarvajanik Utsav Mandal. A 2023 press caption explicitly joins that institution, Dattaram Lad Marg and the Mahaganpati name. FPJ dates the organization to 1956. These identifiers are more reliable than assigning an image from the neighborhood alone; Maharaja and other nearby mandals are separate collections.

ABP Majha documents the 3 August 2025 arrival from a Parel workshop with music, dance and a Govinda salute. Its report focuses on Mazgaon Tadwadi participants building a human-pyramid tribute. This is evidence for that particular procession, rather than proof that its exact arrangement occurs every year.

In August 2026, FPJ described Morya Dhol Tasha Pathak members dressed as BEST transport workers during the arrival procession. It connected their presentation to recognition of the bus workforce. The same report described a Mahalakshmi-form idol. The pathak presentation and the idol theme are related parts of the event, but should not be confused as one sculptural design.

Marathi reports also document practical community activity. Mumbai Live included the mandal among participants in a 2019 CPR and basic-life-support workshop. Maharashtra Times reported a Chief Minister relief-fund contribution during the 2020 lockdown. These dated reports support a service history without projecting every initiative backward to the founding year.

sections.title: A changing idol, with bounded dates

paragraphs.text: The expanded photographic series shows seated forms in 2013-2014, a raised-arm form in 2017, and processional standing forms in 2018-2019 and 2022. The 2013 photograph carries a Vijay Khatu sculptor plaque. Photographer titles and Flickr Taken fields support the annual attributions, but neither later uploads nor costume recognition can independently authenticate exposure dates. A continuous artisan succession remains unestablished.

The 2024 arrival photograph shows a flute and peacock-feather crown; the 2026 image shows a red-clad, lion-supported form described in reporting as Mahalakshmi. These distinct forms belong to the exact Mahaganpati institution in their individual gallery captions. They are not evidence that every similarly named Kalachowki idol belongs to this collection.

On 20 September 2026, Marathi reporting described an electrical accident near a temporary cold-drinks stall opposite the Mahaganpati pandal on Dattaram Lad Marg. Two people died and others were injured. This was preliminary coverage while police investigation continued; differing injury totals and allegations about responsibility are not resolved here.

openQuestions.title: Founding documentation
openQuestions.text: Find an institutional history or registration document confirming the reported 1956 foundation and early organizers.

openQuestions.title: Early visual archive
openQuestions.text: No authenticated earlier-year idol photographs were obtained here. Do not substitute another Kalachowki mandal or a devotional illustration.

openQuestions.title: Artists and yearly forms
openQuestions.text: A verified sequence of sculptors and annually dated idol forms remains to be assembled; one contemporary height is not a permanent specification.

openQuestions.title: Workshop succession
openQuestions.text: The 2013 plaque provides one Vijay Khatu credit. Social-video descriptions mention a later studio change, but no inspected primary annual announcement establishes dates or successor credits, so later artist fields remain empty.

openQuestions.title: Accident documentation
openQuestions.text: Final investigation and differing reported injury counts remain unresolved. A Loksatta follow-up uses an explicitly Gemini-generated illustration, excluded from the photograph archive.

visit.text: The exact street and institutional identity are established by the contemporary immersion caption. Seasonal arrangements and routes require current confirmation.

claims.text: Kalachowkicha Mahaganpati is Kalachowki Vibhag Sarvajanik Utsav Mandal at Dattaram Lad Marg.
The organization is reported as founded in 1956.
The 2025 arrival involved a Mazgaon Tadwadi Govinda salute.
The 2026 arrival featured a Morya Pathak BEST-workforce tribute.
Dated or explicitly annually captioned scene photographs extend the record to 2013, 2014, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2022, 2024 and 2026; early sculptor continuity is not established.

claims.text: Contemporary reporting records two deaths in an electrical accident near the pandal on Dattaram Lad Marg in September 2026; final responsibility is unestablished.

researchNotes.coverage: Expanded independently to ten distinct dated photo years (2013-2026), with photographer caption/Taken metadata separated from contemporary press evidence. Added a visible Vijay Khatu plaque, changing forms, and bounded documentation of the 2026 accident. Founding 1956 remains a retrospective press claim; no original mandal history file located.
